brief.topic: Teardown: the empty state of an AI feature
brief.audience: PMs and designers shipping AI features to users

coreInsight: A blank ‘Ask me anything’ box gets vague asks and vague answers that users judge the feature on, so show starter tasks, an example of a good result and the limits up front.

hooks.text: A blank prompt box is a dead end.
hooks.notes: Concrete UI everyone has seen, with a clear verdict.
Close, but sounds like a rant.

hooks.text: Why nobody uses your AI feature twice.

selectionRationale: Highest total (23/25): a familiar screen with a clear verdict, and the reel shows the fix.

caption.opening: “Ask me anything” sounds open. In practice users type something vague, get something vague back, and decide the feature isn’t for them.
body:
What a good AI first screen shows:
→ Three starter tasks built from the user’s own data
→ One example of a good result
→ What it can’t do yet, in plain words
→ (Behind the scenes) which starters people actually use
The first answer is the onboarding. Design it.

claims.text: Blank, open-ended AI input boxes tend to produce vague requests and weak first answers; starter tasks, an example result and stated limits improve first-use outcomes.
